transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-09-25
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Diego Soto (Redwood SE), Ishan Rao (ZephyrWorks CTO), Maya Chen (ZephyrWorks Infra), Tom Ruiz (ZephyrWorks Product), Sofia Alvarez (ZephyrWorks Security)

Summary:
Planning sync to align on ZephyrWorks listing in Redwood marketplace (hybrid listing path). Focus areas: packaging/helm chart, VPC/KMS and onprem connector, quantization/size constraints for embedded appliances, runbook for canary/UAT and billing/metering expectations. Agree next steps and owners.

Topics Covered:
- Marketplace package format and manifest (helm chart vs OCI bundle)
- Networking/VPC peering, NAT, and CIDR planning for private deployments
- KMS/HSM integration and envelope encryption expectations
- On-prem connector vs fully private stack (quant tradeoffs)
- Telemetry, billing and metering hooks for marketplace listing
- UAT, canary routing and rollback playbooks

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Lena: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we have about 50 minutes, i'll run quick agenda, then pass to marcus for the technical bits.
[00:08] Ishan: hey thanks lena, excited to get this moving, zephyrworks has a handful of customers who need private inference, so marketplace listing will be a big channel for us.
[00:15] Marcus: sweet, i'll start with packaging. for marketplace we support two flavors: a helm chart for onprem/hybrid connectors and an OCI bundle for purely hosted images. for zephyr i'd recommend helm since you need VPC and KMS wiring.
[00:28] Maya: quick clarification — when you say helm chart, do we need to change our docker layout? we have a multi-container appliance: gateway, model-proxy, and metrics sidecar.
[00:36] Marcus: that's fine, helm will let you template multi-container pods. the only thing we ask is that the model server exposes a consistent health endpoint and a metrics endpoint with prometheus labels. also include a readiness probe so the listing can check canary.
[00:48] Tom: ok health + metrics, noted. question on image sizes — some of our model artifacts are huge, will that break the marketplace listing?
[00:55] Diego: good q, marketplace has a recommended limit for initial bundle size for faster installs, we typically surface bigger model artifacts as external downloads. another pattern is to ship a quantized small model in the chart and provide a post-install hook to pull the larger weights if needed.
[01:10] Ishan: ah so you can do a lightweight default model, then let customers opt-in to heavier weights? that's promising. how does that interact with the redwood runtime?
[01:18] Marcus: yep that's the pattern. Redwood's runtime will detect the model variant and pick the appropriate kernel path; we do prefer deterministic naming for model variants in the chart so our autoscaler and routing layers map correctly.
[01:29] Sofia: turning to security, we need to know where keys live. our policy requires KMS-managed keys, and if there's an HSM option that's preferred. what does redwood support?
[01:38] Lena: we support cloud KMS (aws kms, gcp kms) and bring-your-own HSM via an integration layer in the private control plane. for marketplace listing we document both options; the helm values should allow you to plug in KMS endpoints and reference key IDs.
[01:49] Maya: on networking — do you require VPC peering or just simple egress rules? we have strict subnet rules and NAT gateways.
[01:57] Marcus: for hybrid listing we have two connectivity modes: direct VPC peering for lowest latency, or a proxied egress model where the connector initiates a TLS tunnel to the Redwood control plane. both support restricting CIDR ranges. if you want private ingress, peering is the path.
[02:12] Tom: any gotchas on firewall/NAT traversal?
[02:14] Marcus: keep the following open: outbound TLS 443 to our listed endpoints, and an ephemeral range for control-plane health. i'll add exact ports to the checklist. sometimes folks forget DNS resolution for internal registries — if you host images on an internal repo, the node needs to reach it or use an image pull secret from a proxy.
[02:30] Ishan: great. on the compliance front, does the marketplace listing surface audit logs or do we need to wire them?
[02:36] Lena: both. Redwood can send telemetry to your SIEM or you can forward logs via our sidecar. for the listing, we include a telemetry integration doc and a sample fluent bit config. we'll also include a bundle of our SOC2 report and the minimal audit fields we emit.
[02:53] Sofia: perfect. one more — encryption-in-transit for KV cache is mandatory for us. is that in scope?
[02:59] Marcus: yes we encrypt the KV cache in transit and at rest if you enable the data-at-rest flag; the helm values toggle it. there may be minor naming differences in the docs — sometimes the auto-transcripts call it K-V cash — ignore that, it's still cache.
[03:12] Tom: billing and metering — how does the marketplace meter usage? customers want clear unit economics.
[03:18] Lena: the marketplace has two hooks: metering API we call at token/embedding boundaries and optional local counters that sync to our billing aggregator. for hybrid you can run a local meter collector which periodically posts to Redwood's billing endpoint, or use our pull-based reconciliation.
[03:31] Diego: also, plan for meter latency and idempotency. we provide an SDK for safe posting and retry semantics.
[03:36] Maya: so for a disconnected site, we'd buffer usage locally and then ship it when the connection is restored?
[03:41] Marcus: exactly. we support durable buffering with checksums for reconciliation. note that for strict audit customers we also recommend a signed ledger file stored in an object store.
[03:52] Ishan: can we talk about quantization and model compatibility? some of our customers use int8 quant but prefer different kernels.
[03:58] Marcus: Redwood runtime supports q8 and q4 variants on supported architectures; the key is to expose the quant variant in the manifest and label it with the vector size and sequence length characteristics. we'll provide a small compatibility matrix which you can include in the listing.
[04:14] Tom: is there an expectation for us to ship a fallback model if the quantized one underperforms?
[04:19] Lena: recommended, yes. listings often include a fallback to a smaller FP16 variant or delegate to the hosted Redwood model in the cloud to ensure SLA. we can automate fallback routing as part of the rollout policy.
[04:31] Sofia: about rollouts — can we do canary in the marketplace? we want to test on a subset of customers before wider availability.
[04:37] Marcus: yes, we support canary routing: label based and percentage based. for onprem installs, canary is usually a staged upgrade channel that you control; for managed customers we can run a canary in our dedicated environment. we'll provide a sample rollout policy.
[04:50] Ishan: any integration tests you recommend we include in the chart?
[04:54] Diego: include smoke tests that validate health endpoint, metrics scrape, KMS handshake, and a simple inference end-to-end using a small fixture prompt. that's the minimal UAT. we also recommend a long-running load test we can run together in the lab.
[05:09] Tom: would appreciate a checklist.
[05:12] Lena: we'll share the packaging checklist and a sample smoke test script after the call. (link: https://redwood.example.com/marketplace/zephyr-checklist)
[05:20] Marcus: scheduling the lab — i can run a 2-hour session to deploy your helm chart into a staging VPC we control and run reconciliation and metering tests.
[05:28] Maya: that helps. our availability next week is wed/thurs mornings PT.
[05:32] Marcus: i'll send a doodle.
[05:34] Sofia: a note on secrets — we'll want to use secrets manager and not store keys in plain values. is there a recommended pattern?
[05:40] Marcus: yes, helm should reference secrets by name; we support sealed-secrets and external secret operators. for the marketplace we'll include a guide for sealed-secrets and a short example using AWS SSM parameter store.
[05:51] Ishan: anything else on legal/procurement side for listing?
[05:54] Lena: licensing for the chart is standard MIT for the packaging and your model weights are governed by your license. procurement usually wants an SLA addendum if you plan to offer managed services. we'll connect you with our partnerships legal if you need bespoke terms.
[06:07] Tom: final question — do you provide a compatibility badge for listings that pass our integration tests?
[06:11] Lena: yes, once you complete the verification matrix and the lab run, we can mark the listing as Redwood-verified which shows on the marketplace.
[06:20] Marcus: ok quick recap of owners and dates...
[06:23] Lena: lena will send packaging checklist by oct 1, maya will send VPC and KMS choices by sept 30, marcus to propose lab times by sept 29, sofia will enumerate compliance docs by oct 3, tom will draft UAT criteria by oct 2.
[06:39] Ishan: sounds great, thanks everyone. excited to get into the lab.
[06:42] Lena: thanks all, we'll follow up with the links and checklist.

References shared during call:
